industry.why: Neutral, carried, with the disagreement stated: relative strength A (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; A prior) and Logistics B, so the market is buying freight, while the 27-Nov-26 regime (risk-off in the open) is not what a cyclical, freight-exposed industry is paid for over twelve months; no source spoke to transport this week. Nine Pool names here (Kuehne + Nagel, Maersk, Wallenius Wilhelmsen, Hoegh Autoliners, CMB.TECH, NORDEN, Posti, Irish Continental, Wilhelmsen), let through on merit, where their bottom-up grades are the obstacle. Counter-case for higher: three readings at A; for lower: freight is the first casualty if the growth data turn.

sector.why: Neutral, carried, with the disagreement stated: relative strength B (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; A prior), the market buying freight, against a regime that does not pay cyclical freight over twelve months; no source spoke to logistics this week. Nine Pool names let through on merit, where their bottom-up grades are the obstacle (Kuehne + Nagel 27.0, Maersk 12.0, Wallenius Wilhelmsen 23.0 on the Bottom-up composite). Counter-case for higher: three readings at A or B; for lower: freight is the first casualty if the growth data turn.

geography.why: Overweight, from Neutral, on the row's own written condition ('to B if a second source makes the UK case with the rate path read'): Goldman's Sharon Bell (20-Nov) argues 'Domestic not Defensive' with 2027 growth of 1.4% above consensus and the FTSE 100 at a discount with a far higher free-cash-flow yield, James Moberly (23-Nov) has growth improving through 2027 as rates peak, Marshall (22-Nov) has gilts at 4.8% by end-2027, UK core inflation is flat at 2.8% (25-Nov), and Jefferies' Duncan Farr (26-Nov) reads the Financial Policy Committee ruling as favourable for bank cost of equity. 28 Pool stocks are UK-listed and now carry a country weight in Thematic Fit/Momentum; the book holds 16.47 points UK-listed (CVS Group, Fevertree, Hilton Food, Helios Towers). Counter-case: Bell's next two quarters are 'tough', the Bank of England's decision is still unread, Oppenheimer underweights Europe as a whole, and the UK Pool names are mostly global businesses. Back to C if the Bank of England's guidance is read hawkish or a UK consumer reading arrives falling.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
